act.name: Code on Wages, 2019
act.source_name: Official Gazette of India / India Code
act.source_authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
act.supersedes: Payment of Wages Act, 1936 / Minimum Wages Act, 1948 / Payment of Bonus Act, 1965
act.description: An Act to consolidate and amend the laws relating to wages and bonus and matters connected therewith. Subsumes the Payment of Wages Act 1936 and Minimum Wages Act 1948.

sections.title: Time limit for payment of wages and final settlement upon termination
sections.text:
(1) All wages shall be paid in current coin or currency notes or by cheque or by crediting to bank account of the employee.
(2) Where an employee has been removed or dismissed from service, or retrenched or has resigned from service, or became unemployed due to closure of the establishment, the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his removal, dismissal, retrenchment or resignation.
sections.plain_language_summary: Employer must pay all pending wages and final settlement within 2 working days of resignation or termination.

sections.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
sections.text:
(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, there shall be no deduction made from the wages of an employee except those authorised under this Code.
(2) Deductions from wages may be made only for absence from duty, damage to or loss of goods expressly entrusted to the employee, housing accommodation provided by employer, or advances given.
sections.plain_language_summary: Employers cannot make unauthorized deductions from employee salaries except for specified statutory items or advances.

sections.title: Claims under Code and procedure thereof.
sections.chapter: Chapter VI - Payment of Dues, Claims and Audit
sections.text:
(1) The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint one or more authorities to hear and determine claims arising out of non-payment of minimum wages or illegal deduction from wages or delay in payment of wages.
(2) The application for claim may be filed by the employee or any trade union within a period of three years from the date on which the claim arose.
sections.plain_language_summary: Employees can file a claim before the Labour Authority for unpaid salary or illegal deductions within 3 years.
